stem: A student with type 1 diabetes returns to school after the diabetes care team changes the student’s insulin regimen and continuous glucose monitor settings. Which action by the school nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Obtain and implement an updated individualized Diabetes Medical Management Plan (DMMP) that reflects the student’s current monitoring, insulin, hypo/hyperglycemia, and emergency-care instructions.
options.B: Continue using the prior DMMP until the next school year because diabetes plans are updated only annually.
options.C: Replace the individualized DMMP with the school’s general diabetes policy because one district-wide plan is sufficient for every student.
options.D: Keep the revised diabetes instructions only for the school nurse and avoid communicating applicable emergency procedures to trained school personnel.

rationale: A is correct. Current ADA school guidance states that each student with diabetes should have an individualized DMMP developed by the health care professional in collaboration with the student and parent or guardian. The DMMP is the basis for school diabetes care and emergency planning and should be updated annually or whenever the student’s regimen, self-management level, or school circumstances change. B delays a required update after a treatment change. C ignores the individualized medical orders. D is unsafe because appropriate school personnel need training and access to the instructions necessary to provide care and respond to emergencies.
educational_objective: Coordinate safe school diabetes care by ensuring the student’s individualized DMMP is updated whenever the diabetes regimen changes and that relevant trained school personnel can follow the current monitoring, treatment, and emergency instructions.
source_document_title: Diabetes Care in the School Setting: A Statement of the American Diabetes Association; Diabetes Medical Management Plan; Children and Adolescents: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026

source_claim_supported: Students with diabetes require an individualized DMMP that guides monitoring, treatment, and emergency care at school and should be updated when the diabetes regimen or relevant circumstances change.

The final version tests the current ADA requirement to update an individualized DMMP when care changes, while preserving its core monitoring, insulin, hypo/hyperglycemia, and emergency-care functions.

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the ADA 2024 school statement, updated 2025 DMMP resource, and 2026 Standards of Care school section. All support individualized plans and update when treatment changes.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A is directly supported and does not invent school-specific staffing, delegation, or legal requirements beyond communicating applicable instructions to trained personnel.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; a regimen/technology change requires an updated individualized plan.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; annual review is not the only trigger for updating the DMMP.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; a generic district policy does not replace individualized medical orders.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; safe school care requires trained personnel to know and implement relevant current instructions and emergency procedures.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A ensures that current treatment orders are reflected in the plan used at school.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern plan management after a real change in care.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is directly aligned because the construct is coordination and communication of an individualized plan across settings.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked DMMP versus 504/IEP distinction, annual-versus-change update triggers, school nurse role, trained personnel communication, current 2026 school guidance, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
